title: Dynamism and evolvability in nucleic acid enzymes
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76473-9

Dynamism and evolvability link enzyme flexibility to adaptive potential, yet how these concepts apply to nucleic acid enzymes is largely unexplored. Here the authors compare the evolution of threose nucleic acids (TNA) and DNA-based enzymes, and show the rigid TNA backbone limits adaptability.

title: Tunable arbitrarily located quasi-corner states in multiphase weak topological insulator
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76594-1

Despite interest in higher-order topological insulating phases in photonic devices, their characterisation beyond conventional symmetry assumptions is incomplete. Here, the authors introduce 0D quasi-corner states located at defects and desirable edges of 2D anisotropic honeycomb lattices in photonic structures, advancing symmetry characterisation and control.

title: Enhancing iNKT cell immunotherapy through the integration of optimized CAR endodomains and iNKT engagers
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76718-7

iNKT cells are a subset of T cells with both innate and adaptive features, emerging as a promising immunotherapy platform due to their rapid response. Here, the authors develop a CAR-iNKT strategy incorporating a CD28ζ co-stimulatory domain and two bispecific iNKT engagers to enhance multiple myeloma targeting.

title: Epigenetic repression of IL-1β by C1QBP restricts Dectin-1-mediated host defense against murine invasive candidiasis
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76756-1

Engagement of Dectin-1 on dendritic cells drives IL-1β production and is a critical component of the immune response to invasive candidiasis. Here the authors show epigenetic repression of IL-1β by a complement binding protein can restrain the dectin1 driven immune response in a murine model of invasive candidiasis.

title: Determinants of functional burden pleiotropy and gene dosage responses across human traits
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76676-0

Gene dosage can help explain comorbidities in developmental pediatric and psychiatric disorders. Here, the authors map how rare copy-number variants disrupting tissue and cell-type gene sets shape 43 human traits.

title: Yu-Shiba-Rusinov-assisted Andreev transport in a molecular junction between superconductors
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76478-4

Magnetic impurities and weak links create distinct subgap excitations in superconductors. Here, the authors tune a nickelocene/Fe junction on Pb to show that combined Yu-Shiba-Rusinov (YSR) and multiple-Andreev-reflection (MAR) processes explain shifted subgap features and the onset of Josephson transport.

title: TogoPhosTAC as a delivery-ready platform for targeted protein dephosphorylation
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76725-8

This study presents togoPhosTAC, a biologic platform that directs engineered phosphatases to target proteins for phosphate removal, reducing pathological tau phosphorylation and alleviating behavioral deficits in male PS19 tauopathy mice.

title: Eradication of MRSA biofilm-associated implant infections by low-immunogenic sustained-release lysostaphin fused to thermosensitive polypeptides
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76664-4

Authors present an antimicrobial characterisation of their elastin-like polypeptide-fused lysostaphin, which offers enhanced stability, low immunogenicity and sustained release via injection. It safely and completely eradicates in vivo MRSA biofilm infections, outperforming lysostaphin and vancomycin.
